purpose: Explain which verified property interests changed, remained unchanged or remain unresolved because of an approved timeline event, using before-state, event, legal rule, registration/effect evidence and after-state.
rules: An event is not itself proof of its legal effect.
Each property-interest dimension is assessed independently.
A change in one interest does not imply a change in another.
Registration effect is distinguished from signing, execution or possession.
Inheritance does not automatically establish registered transfer.
Sale does not automatically establish mortgage discharge.
A court order's effect depends on its scope and applicable registration/legal framework.
Easement or boundary events do not automatically transfer ownership.
Unchanged means no material change identified within the verified evidence scope.
Where before or after state is incomplete, the limitation remains visible.
hard_stops: Never infer after-state from event name alone.
Never label every event an ownership change.
Never infer discharge from sale or inheritance without evidence.
Never infer registration from execution or signing.
Never infer a legal effect without the applicable legal source.
Never hide an unresolved interest dimension.
Never create a new legal conclusion during display rendering.
